newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-Ferro to grow above industry trend.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Ferro to grow above industry trend.

text.p: Specialty chemicals company Ferro Corp will continue the restructuring it started in 1991 and is now confident it can grow its core powder coatings business at more than the annual six percent industry average.
Chief executive Albert Bersticker told Reuters in an interview that Ferro had turned around its key powder coatings division and was looking at potential acquisitions.
"In 1994 and 1995, Ferro was seriously asking whether we wanted to be in this business at all. I have changed my mind," Bersticker told Reuters.

Ferro's coatings are already used on products such as home appliances and its coatings, colors and ceramics division contributed $202 million to sales of $342 million in the first quarter of 1997 and $781 million of 1996's 1.35 billion.
Technological improvements mean Ferro is on the verge of commercializing a paint for the top coat of cars, displacing environmentally harmful solvent-based paints.

Proprietary technology will also enable paints to cure at lower temperatures and open up new uses for wood and plastics, which Bersticker believes will start to be seen in earnings from the end of this year.

"In the past year, return on net assets has gone from single to double digits, in 1995 we were at breakeven, in 1996 operating margins were two percent and in 1997 they will be four to five percent," he said.
Bersticker said that while Ferro is still rationalizing and will close 30 operating units, mostly in its glass business by 1999, it is now strong enough to look at acquisitions.
"We could make a very, very sizeable acquisition but we want to stay with our area of core competence and we do not want long-term dilution of earnings," he said.

He is looking at powder coatings in Europe and possibly a purchase in the U.S., which Bersticker believes could avoid Federal Trade Commission approval because the market is so fragmented, and a small deal in South America.
Ferro paid $57 million for ICI Plc's Glidden paints business in 1993 and some analysts said the money would have been better spent buying back shares, rather than invested in a low margin business.
"We had not realized the returns we should have achieved, but it is starting to pay off now," Bersticker said.
The company's target return on net assets is 23 percent and he conceded the powder business is not yet hitting that.
"We are not where we want to be, we fall below the mid-level in our peer group and want to be in the top half in 18 months," Bersticker said.

The company has a car paints venture with DuPont Co which it believes will help it compete with new entrants in powder paints for cars from companies which have a strong presence in the auto-paints business such as PPG Industries Inc, Sherwin-Williams and Valspar Corp .
"Ferro has the leading edge. We have a unit dedicated exclusively to that business and it will be a huge market for Ferro," Bersticker said. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
